title: Choosing a count distribution
text: washington_roads data contain crashes 507 road segments, observed three years (1501 rows). model total crashes function traffic volume (lnaadt) speed-limit indicator speed50, logarithm segment length offset. models overview treat every row independent; repeated observations segments modelled vignette("random-parameters--panels", package = "flexCountReg").

what: Fitting candidate families on the same rows
title: Choosing a count distribution
text: countreg() takes distribution family. Gradient-based optimizers (method = "BFGS" "NR") usually fastest choice closed-form families. models use rows, log-likelihoods comparable. NB1 NB2 differ extra variance grows mean; Polya-Aeppli family PA (Poisson-Tweedie distribution, variance μ+ϕμ1.5\mu + \phi\mu^{1.5}) lies , Delaporte family mixes Poisson negative binomial component.
code: f <- Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + speed50 fit <- function(family) {   countreg(f, data = washington_roads, family = family, offset = "lnlength",            method = "BFGS") } models <- list(   Poisson = fit("Poisson"),   NB1 = fit("NB1"),   NB2 = fit("NB2"),   PIG1 = fit("PIG1"),   GP1 = fit("GP1"),   PA = fit("PA"),   DELAPORTE = fit("DELAPORTE") ) sapply(models, nobs) #>   Poisson       NB1       NB2      PIG1       GP1        PA DELAPORTE  #>      1501      1501      1501      1501      1501      1501      1501

title: Choosing a count distribution
text: glance() gives one row fit statistics per model: NB2 lowest AIC, NB2, PA, DELAPORTE within 2 AIC units , difference small choose basis alone. families whose variance proportional mean (NB1, PIG1, GP1) least 12.8 AIC units behind best model: extra variance grows faster mean data. parameters can also weakly identified. Delaporte model’s share shape parameters large standard errors : data separate Poisson negative binomial components Delaporte distribution; offers advantage NB2.

title: Choosing a count distribution
text: Three summaries often used choose distribution fitting anything. None sufficient : unconditional variance--mean ratio (2.19) mixes variation explained covariates variation left . fitting covariates Poisson Pearson dispersion 1.35: overdispersion, less raw ratio suggests. large share zeros (73% ) evidence separate zero process: fitted Poisson model already expects 72% zeros. Compare observed zeros expected fitted model. AIC ranking tells fitted models closest data among tried. Small differences decisive, model best -sample necessarily best predicting new data; held-comparison shown vignette("diagnosing-count-models", package = "flexCountReg").
code: y <- washington_roads$Total_crashes pearson <- function(m) {   sum(residuals(m, type = "pearson")^2) / (nobs(m) - length(coef(m))) } expected_zeros <- sapply(models[c("Poisson", "NB2")], function(m)   mean(predict(m, type = "prob", max_count = 0)[, 1])) c(variance_to_mean = var(y) / mean(y),   pearson_poisson = pearson(models$Poisson),   observed_zeros = mean(y == 0),   expected_zeros_poisson = expected_zeros[["Poisson"]],   expected_zeros_nb2 = expected_zeros[["NB2"]]) #>       variance_to_mean        pearson_poisson         observed_zeros  #>              2.1873535              1.3485030              0.7335110  #> expected_zeros_poisson     expected_zeros_nb2  #>              0.7212261              0.7378874

what: Does the model reproduce the counts?
title: Choosing a count distribution
text: Information criteria rank models, show model fails. rootogram compares observed frequency count frequency expected fitted model, square-root scale. Bars hang expected curve; bar ends zero means count -predicted, one ends zero means -predicted.  Randomized quantile residuals approximately standard normal model correct, count distribution, normal Q-Q plot useful check (residuals randomized, seed set):  CURE plot (cumulative residuals covariate) checks mean model along covariate; bounds assume independent residuals:
code: oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) rootogram(models$Poisson, main = "Poisson") rootogram(models$NB2, main = "NB2") par(oldpar) set.seed(1) oldpar <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) for (nm in c("Poisson", "NB2")) {   r <- residuals(models[[nm]], type = "quantile")   qqnorm(r, main = nm, pch = 20, col = "grey40")   abline(0, 1, lty = 2) } par(oldpar) cureplot(models$NB2, indvar = "lnaadt")

The estimate may be on the boundary of the #> parameter space or not at a maximum. pi_zero <- unname(plogis(coef(zinb)["Zero:(Intercept)"])) c(NB2 = as.numeric(logLik(models$NB2)), ZINB = as.numeric(logLik(zinb)),   zero_probability = pi_zero) #>              NB2             ZINB zero_probability  #>    -1.090559e+03    -1.090560e+03     4.338153e-05

title: Preparing count data: exposure, offsets, weights and missing values
text: question covariate x changes rate events per unit exposure. row one independent unit (example road segment, patient-year plot) observed known exposure, y number events exposure. data simulated Yi∼Poisson(μi),μi=exposurei×exp⁡(−0.5+0.6xi),Y_i \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_i), \qquad   \mu_i = \text{exposure}_i \times \exp(-0.5 + 0.6\,x_i), true rate per unit exposure exp⁡(−0.5+0.6x)\exp(-0.5 + 0.6x).

title: Preparing count data: exposure, offsets, weights and missing values
text: Taking logs mean model gives log⁡μi=log⁡(exposurei)+β0+β1xi,\log\mu_i = \log(\text{exposure}_i) + \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_i, log exposure enters linear predictor coefficient fixed 1: offset. two equivalent ways supply . Use one fit, : agree glm(): estimates close true values (-0.5 0.6). Giving forms error, ambiguous whether exposure count twice:
code: # 1. offset() in the formula, with the exposure on its original scale m_formula <- countreg(y ~ x + offset(log(exposure)), data = d,                       family = "POISSON", method = "BFGS") # 2. the `offset` argument, naming a column that is already logged m_column <- countreg(y ~ x, data = d, family = "POISSON",                      offset = "log_exposure", method = "BFGS") rbind(formula = coef(m_formula), column = coef(m_column)) #>         (Intercept)         x #> formula   -0.542581 0.6455173 #> column    -0.542581 0.6455173 all.equal(coef(m_formula), coef(m_column)) #> [1] TRUE coef(glm(y ~ x + offset(log(exposure)), data = d, family = poisson())) #> (Intercept)           x  #>  -0.5425810   0.6455173 tryCatch(countreg(y ~ x + offset(log(exposure)), data = d,                   family = "POISSON", offset = "log_exposure"),          error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)) #> [1] "Specify the offset either with offset() in the formula or with the `offset` argument, not both."

text: Data sometimes stored compactly, one row per distinct combination values column counting many observations share . weights argument treats row many independent observations: compact fit frequency weights fit expanded data model: Estimates, log-likelihood, standard errors BIC agree. what: Missing values and the analysis sample
title: Preparing count data: exposure, offsets, weights and missing values
text: countreg() uses rows complete every variable model needs: response, mean covariates, offset, weights variables distribution-parameter, zero underreporting formula. model components therefore use rows. illustrate, simulate overdispersed count y_nb (negative binomial, NB2 dispersion 0.5) make x missing two rows second covariate z, used model dispersion parameter, missing three: rows fit used stored model, dropped rows can listed (position data; id column used report , predictor):
code: dm <- d dm$y_nb <- rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = dm$exposure * exp(-0.5 + 0.6 * dm$x)) dm$z <- rnorm(n) dm$x[c(4, 9)] <- NA dm$z[c(9, 15, 22)] <- NA m_mean <- countreg(y_nb ~ x + offset(log(exposure)), data = dm, family = "NB2",                    method = "BFGS") #> 2 row(s) with missing values were removed. m_disp <- countreg(y_nb ~ x + offset(log(exposure)), data = dm, family = "NB2",                    dis_param_formula_1 = ~ z, method = "BFGS") #> 4 row(s) with missing values were removed. c(mean_model = nobs(m_mean), dispersion_model = nobs(m_disp)) #>       mean_model dispersion_model  #>              398              396 dm$id[setdiff(seq_len(nrow(dm)), m_mean$model$rows_used)] #> [1] 4 9 dm$id[setdiff(seq_len(nrow(dm)), m_disp$model$rows_used)] #> [1]  4  9 15 22

title: Diagnosing a count model and deciding what to change
text: Question: fitted model fail, change fix ? Three counts simulated 600 units, function one covariate x:
code: set.seed(101) n <- 600 x <- runif(n, -1.5, 1.5) sim <- data.frame(   x = x,   y_ok = rpois(n, exp(0.5 + 0.8 * x)),   y_curve = rpois(n, exp(0.3 + 0.8 * x + 0.6 * x^2)),   y_disp = rnbinom(n, size = 1 / 0.8, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.8 * x)))  ok <- countreg(y_ok ~ x, data = sim, family = "POISSON", method = "BFGS") curve_lin <- countreg(y_curve ~ x, data = sim, family = "POISSON",                       method = "BFGS") disp_pois <- countreg(y_disp ~ x, data = sim, family = "POISSON",                       method = "BFGS")

what: A first summary: the Pearson dispersion
title: Diagnosing a count model and deciding what to change
text: Pearson statistic divided residual degrees freedom near 1 mean variance right: problems inflate . large value says something wrong, : misspecified mean leaves systematic structure residuals, also looks like extra variance. diagnostics separate two.
code: pearson <- function(fit) {   sum(residuals(fit, type = "pearson")^2) / (nobs(fit) - length(coef(fit))) } round(c(ok = pearson(ok), curve = pearson(curve_lin),         dispersion = pearson(disp_pois)), 2) #>         ok      curve dispersion  #>       1.08       1.71       2.70

code: co <- coef(rp) patient <- epil[epil$subject == 1, ] x_fixed <- as.vector(model.matrix(~ -1 + progabide + lbase + lage + V4,                                   patient) %*%                        co[c("progabide", "lbase", "lage", "V4")]) size <- 1 / exp(co[["ln(alpha)"]])           # NB2: Var = mu + alpha mu^2 mu_b <- co[["(Intercept):Mean"]] sd_b <- abs(co[["(Intercept):St.Dev"]]) set.seed(42) R <- 20000 # joint: one intercept per simulated patient, shared by the four periods b <- rnorm(R, mu_b, sd_b) joint <- rowSums(sapply(1:4, function(t)   rnbinom(R, size = size, mu = exp(b + x_fixed[t])))) # independent: a new intercept for every period (wrong for one patient) indep <- rowSums(sapply(1:4, function(t)   rnbinom(R, size = size, mu = exp(rnorm(R, mu_b, sd_b) + x_fixed[t])))) rbind(joint = c(mean = mean(joint), sd = sd(joint),                 quantile(joint, c(0.05, 0.95)), P_over_40 = mean(joint > 40)),       independent = c(mean = mean(indep), sd = sd(indep),                       quantile(indep, c(0.05, 0.95)),                       P_over_40 = mean(indep > 40))) #>                 mean       sd 5% 95% P_over_40 #> joint       13.29395 8.383284  3  29    0.0114 #> independent 13.26105 5.678857  5  24    0.0008 sum(predict(rp, newdata = patient, method = "Exact")) #> [1] 13.2995

Every row gets fold, recorded table row identifier: model refit training folds , including everything estimated data (factor levels fixed, every level every factor occurs every training set): (level missing training set, predict() stop rather invent coefficient ; split redone level merged.) candidates use folds held-rows. held-child, --fold table records prediction, log probability observed count predicted probability zero. Failed non-converged fits recorded, dropped: log score uses probability actual held-count, read column count (probabilities run largest held-count, count falls outside ).
code: q <- MASS::quine q$row_id <- seq_len(nrow(q)) set.seed(2026) K <- 5 q$fold <- sample(rep(seq_len(K), length.out = nrow(q))) table(q$fold) #>  #>  1  2  3  4  5  #> 30 29 29 29 29 all(sapply(seq_len(K), function(k) {   tr <- q[q$fold != k, ]   all(sapply(c("Eth", "Sex", "Age", "Lrn"), function(v)     all(table(tr[[v]]) > 0))) })) #> [1] TRUE f <- Days ~ Eth + Sex + Age + Lrn families <- c("POISSON", "NB2") oof <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(K), function(k) {   train <- q[q$fold != k, ]   test <- q[q$fold == k, ]   do.call(rbind, lapply(families, function(fam) {     fit <- tryCatch(countreg(f, data = train, family = fam,                              method = "BFGS"),                     error = function(e) NULL)     ok <- !is.null(fit) && isTRUE(fit$model$converged)     if (!ok) {       return(data.frame(row_id = test$row_id, fold = k, family = fam,                         y = test$Days, mu = NA, log_p = NA, p_zero = NA,                         status = "fit failed"))     }     P <- predict(fit, newdata = test, type = "prob",                  max_count = max(test$Days))     data.frame(row_id = test$row_id, fold = k, family = fam,                y = test$Days, mu = predict(fit, newdata = test),                log_p = log(P[cbind(seq_len(nrow(test)), test$Days + 1)]),                p_zero = P[, 1], status = "ok")   })) })) head(oof) #>   row_id fold  family  y       mu      log_p       p_zero status #> 1      1    1 POISSON  2 29.54024 -23.461884 1.481955e-13     ok #> 2      4    1 POISSON  5 21.55623 -10.990394 4.347608e-10     ok #> 3      5    1 POISSON  5 21.55623 -10.990394 4.347608e-10     ok #> 4      8    1 POISSON 22 21.55623  -2.472784 4.347608e-10     ok #> 5     17    1 POISSON 57 31.11360 -11.563683 3.072810e-14     ok #> 6     20    1 POISSON 16 22.70434  -3.415303 1.379210e-10     ok table(oof$family, oof$status) #>           #>            ok #>   NB2     146 #>   POISSON 146

V4 marks fourth visit. (data MASS 7.3-65 later include documented correction one count.) pooled model treats 236 rows independent; random-effects model (renb(), negative binomial model Hausman, Hall Griliches, 1984) gives patient shared effect: pooled model’s standard error treatment effect 0.101, 0.143 panel model. what: 2. A generator that can be checked
title: Simulation studies for count models
text: data generated base R’s rpois() rnbinom(), generator independent code evaluated: Two checks independent results. First, α=1\alpha = 1 NB2 distribution geometric, generator’s frequencies must match dgeom(): Second, package’s simulate() method, used later fitted models, must reproduce NB2 mean variance fitted parameters: ratios centred 1, spread expected 2,000 draws.
code: generate <- function(sc) {   x <- rnorm(sc$n)   t <- runif(sc$n, 0.5, 2)   mu <- t * exp(sc$beta0 + sc$beta_x * x)   y <- if (sc$family == "POISSON") rpois(sc$n, mu) else     rnbinom(sc$n, size = 1 / sc$alpha, mu = mu)   data.frame(y, x, log_t = log(t)) } set.seed(1) draws <- rnbinom(1e5, size = 1, mu = 2) round(rbind(simulated = tabulate(draws + 1, 6) / 1e5,             geometric = dgeom(0:5, prob = 1 / 3)), 4) #>             [,1]   [,2]   [,3]   [,4]   [,5]   [,6] #> simulated 0.3318 0.2232 0.1480 0.0987 0.0656 0.0436 #> geometric 0.3333 0.2222 0.1481 0.0988 0.0658 0.0439 set.seed(2) d <- generate(scenarios[scenarios$family == "NB2" & scenarios$n == 400, ]) fit <- countreg(y ~ x + offset(log_t), data = d, family = "NB2",                 method = "BFGS") sims <- simulate(fit, nsim = 2000, seed = 3) mu <- predict(fit) alpha <- exp(coef(fit)[["ln(alpha)"]]) summary(data.frame(mean_ratio = rowMeans(sims) / mu,                    var_ratio = apply(sims, 1, var) / (mu + alpha * mu^2))) #>    mean_ratio       var_ratio      #>  Min.   :0.9178   Min.   :0.8341   #>  1st Qu.:0.9855   1st Qu.:0.9678   #>  Median :1.0014   Median :1.0038   #>  Mean   :1.0008   Mean   :1.0048   #>  3rd Qu.:1.0173   3rd Qu.:1.0403   #>  Max.   :1.0688   Max.   :1.1824

title: Simulation studies for count models
text: replicate generates one dataset, applies procedure, returns one row per procedure. Failures warnings recorded, dropped:
code: fit_one <- function(d, family) {   warn <- character(0)   m <- tryCatch(     withCallingHandlers(       countreg(y ~ x + offset(log_t), data = d, family = family,                method = "BFGS"),       warning = function(w) {         warn <<- c(warn, conditionMessage(w))         invokeRestart("muffleWarning")       }),     error = function(e) e)   if (inherits(m, "error")) {     return(data.frame(estimate = NA, se = NA, status = "error",                       note = conditionMessage(m)))   }   co <- summary(m)$coefficients   status <- if (!isTRUE(m$model$converged)) "not converged" else     if (length(warn)) "warning" else "ok"   data.frame(estimate = co["x", 1], se = co["x", 2], status = status,              note = paste(warn, collapse = "; ")) }  one_replicate <- function(sc, rep) {   d <- generate(sc)   out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("POISSON", "NB2"), function(proc)     cbind(scenario = sc$id, rep = rep, procedure = proc, fit_one(d, proc))))   out$truth <- sc$beta_x   out }

what: 6. Panel data: keep the independent unit
title: Simulation studies for count models
text: repeated measurements, independent unit group, generator must give rows group one shared effect. , 100 units observed 5 times, gamma-distributed unit effect (mean 1, variance 0.5), unit-level covariate zz row-level covariate xx: negative multinomial model negmultinom() (family "NM2", default) matches process: Poisson counts given gamma unit effect mean 1 variance α\alpha (0.5), shared rows unit. pooled Poisson model ignores grouping: pooled model’s standard error unit-level covariate zz far spread estimates, intervals undercover; negative multinomial model accounts shared effect. Bootstrap cross-validation study must also resample whole units, never rows (stderr = "boot" panel models ).
code: generate_panel <- function(n_units = 100, T = 5, theta = 0.5) {   id <- rep(seq_len(n_units), each = T)   u <- rgamma(n_units, shape = 1 / theta, rate = 1 / theta)[id]   z <- rnorm(n_units)[id]   x <- rnorm(n_units * T)   data.frame(id, z, x, y = rpois(n_units * T, u * exp(0.2 + 0.4 * z +                                                         0.3 * x))) } panel_rep <- function(r) {   assign(".Random.seed", panel_streams[[r]], envir = globalenv())   d <- generate_panel()   est <- function(m, nm) {     co <- summary(m)$coefficients     c(estimate = co[nm, 1], se = co[nm, 2])   }   pooled <- countreg(y ~ z + x, data = d, family = "POISSON",                      method = "BFGS")   nm <- negmultinom(y ~ z + x, group_var = "id", data = d)   rbind(data.frame(rep = r, procedure = "pooled Poisson",                    term = c("z", "x"),                    rbind(est(pooled, "z"), est(pooled, "x")),                    converged = pooled$model$converged),         data.frame(rep = r, procedure = "negative multinomial",                    term = c("z", "x"), rbind(est(nm, "z"), est(nm, "x")),                    converged = nm$model$converged)) } R_panel <- 100 panel_streams <- make_streams(R_panel) panel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(R_panel), panel_rep)) panel$truth <- ifelse(panel$term == "z", 0.4, 0.3) panel$cover <- abs(panel$estimate - panel$truth) <=   qnorm(0.975) * panel$se aggregate(cbind(estimate, se, cover, converged) ~ procedure + term,           data = panel, FUN = mean) #>              procedure term  estimate         se cover converged #> 1 negative multinomial    x 0.3026586 0.04191190  0.94         1 #> 2       pooled Poisson    x 0.3004392 0.03796208  0.88         1 #> 3 negative multinomial    z 0.4021180 0.08419030  0.98         1 #> 4       pooled Poisson    z 0.3933019 0.03882494  0.72         1 aggregate(estimate ~ procedure + term, data = panel, FUN = sd) #>              procedure term   estimate #> 1 negative multinomial    x 0.04688169 #> 2       pooled Poisson    x 0.05319242 #> 3 negative multinomial    z 0.07529461 #> 4       pooled Poisson    z 0.07446998

code: recover_one <- function(seed, gamma) {   d <- simulate_reports(2000, seed, gamma)   warned <- FALSE   m <- tryCatch(withCallingHandlers(     countreg(y ~ x, data = d, family = "NB2", underreport_formula = ~ w,              method = "BFGS"),     warning = function(w) {       warned <<- TRUE       invokeRestart("muffleWarning")     }), error = function(e) NULL)   if (is.null(m) || !isTRUE(m$model$converged)) {     return(c(NA, NA, NA, NA, converged = 0, warned = warned))   }   co <- coef(m)[c("(Intercept)", "x", "Underreporting:(Intercept)",                   "Underreporting:w")]   c(co, converged = 1, warned = warned) } recovery <- lapply(designs, function(g)   t(sapply(101:120, recover_one, gamma = g))) truth <- function(g) c(1, 0.5, g) recovery_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(designs), function(k) {   r <- recovery[[k]]   ok <- r[, "converged"] == 1   data.frame(design = k,              parameter = c("(Intercept)", "x", "Rep:(Intercept)", "Rep:w"),              truth = truth(designs[[k]]),              mean = colMeans(r[ok, 1:4]),              median = apply(r[ok, 1:4], 2, median),              sd = apply(r[ok, 1:4], 2, sd),              converged = sum(ok), warned = sum(r[, "warned"]),              row.names = NULL) })) recovery_table[, 4:6] <- round(recovery_table[, 4:6], 3) recovery_table #>   design       parameter truth   mean median    sd converged warned #> 1   weak     (Intercept)   1.0  1.167  1.019 0.525        20     11 #> 2   weak               x   0.5  0.501  0.505 0.024        20     11 #> 3   weak Rep:(Intercept)   1.5  1.501  1.295 1.573        20     11 #> 4   weak           Rep:w  -2.0 -2.217 -1.820 1.063        20     11 #> 5 strong     (Intercept)   1.0  0.990  0.974 0.084        20      0 #> 6 strong               x   0.5  0.504  0.508 0.024        20      0 #> 7 strong Rep:(Intercept)   3.0  3.102  2.977 0.671        20      0 #> 8 strong           Rep:w  -5.0 -5.097 -4.907 0.705        20      0

text: Three datasets 1,000 counts covariate x simulated: ordinary NB2 count, zero-inflated NB2 count (25% structural zeros) hurdle count. three many zeros: dataset, fit NB2, zero-inflated NB2 hurdle NB2 constant zero model, compare AIC: lowest AIC row belongs NB2, ZINB, hurdle (ordinary, zero-inflated hurdle data turn). ordinary count, estimated structural-zero probability small (0.032) extra parameter costs AIC. zero-inflated data, 25% structural zeros 1,000 rows, zero-inflated model improves AIC NB2 3.7: NB2 distribution larger dispersion can reproduce much zero share. Real zero processes rarely clean , expect small differences.
code: set.seed(12) n <- 1000 x <- rnorm(n) mu <- exp(0.3 + 0.5 * x) y_nb <- rnbinom(n, size = 1, mu = mu) y_zi <- ifelse(runif(n) < 0.25, 0, rnbinom(n, size = 1, mu = mu)) # hurdle: positive with probability 0.55, then a zero-truncated NB2 count draw_pos <- function(m) { repeat { v <- rnbinom(1, size = 1, mu = m)   if (v > 0) return(v) } } y_h <- ifelse(runif(n) < 0.55, vapply(mu, draw_pos, 0), 0) sims <- data.frame(x, y_nb, y_zi, y_h) sapply(sims[-1], function(y) mean(y == 0)) #>  y_nb  y_zi   y_h  #> 0.417 0.585 0.445 fit_three <- function(resp) {   f <- reformulate("x", resp)   list(NB2 = countreg(f, data = sims, family = "NB2", method = "BFGS"),        ZINB = suppressWarnings(          countreg(f, data = sims, family = "NB2", zero_formula = ~ 1,                   method = "BFGS")),        hurdle = countreg(f, data = sims, family = "NB2", zero_formula = ~ 1,                          zero_type = "hurdle", method = "BFGS")) } sim_fits <- lapply(c(ordinary = "y_nb", zero_inflated = "y_zi",                      hurdle = "y_h"), fit_three) aic <- t(sapply(sim_fits, function(m) sapply(m, AIC))) round(aic, 1) #>                  NB2   ZINB hurdle #> ordinary      3303.8 3305.7 3352.6 #> zero_inflated 2704.1 2700.5 2727.1 #> hurdle        3205.6 3205.0 3192.8

title: Estimation of a Variety of Count Regression Models
text: goal flexCountReg provide functions allow analyst estimate count regression models can handle multiple analysis issues, including: many count distributions beyond Poisson negative binomial (see list ), distribution parameter modeled function variables (generalized count models); underreporting, zero-inflated hurdle versions every distribution; random parameters, heterogeneity means variances, exact, simulated Empirical Bayes (observation-specific) predictions; random-effects panel models (negative binomial, Poisson-Lindley, negative multinomial); finite mixtures latent-class count regressions, constant, covariate-dependent known class proportions, shared class-specific parameters, different families different classes, one class per panel; model comparison diagnostics: likelihood-ratio tests, comparison tables, marginal effects, CURE plots, rootograms randomized quantile residuals; interactive app (launch_app()) whole workflow, data downloadable R script reproduces analysis. Fitted models work standard R generics (coef(), vcov(), AIC(), BIC(), confint(), predict(), simulate(), update(), …), tidy(), glance() augment(), tidymodels count_reg() parsnip model.

title: Estimation of a Variety of Count Regression Models
text: Model Estimation Functions countreg() estimates cross-sectional count regression models distributions , optional models distribution parameters, underreporting, zero-inflated hurdle zero models. countreg_rp() estimates random parameters count models, optionally panels, correlated random parameters, heterogeneity means variances random parameters. countreg_mix() countreg_lc() estimate finite-mixture latent-class count models (engine two vocabularies), several reproducible starts, component_probs() / class_probs() give prior posterior class probabilities. renb() estimates random effects negative binomial regression model. poisLind.re() (also poislind_re()) estimates random effects Poisson-Lindley model. negmultinom() estimates negative multinomial (random effects) panel models (NM1, NM2 NM-P). repois() estimates random effects Poisson model gamma random effect. count_reg() parsnip model specification "flexCountReg" engine, use tidymodels (distribution can tuned count_family()). Working Fitted Models summary() gives coefficient table, standard-error type, fit statistics likelihood-ratio test Poisson model. predict() gives expected counts (one per row newdata, NA incomplete rows), probability count, components underreporting zero models. countreg() models also gives confidence intervals expected count prediction intervals new count (interval = "confidence" "prediction"). random parameters models offers exact, simulated Empirical Bayes ("Individual") predictions. tolerance_interval() gives content tolerance intervals countreg() models: count ranges intended contain least stated share outcome distribution stated confidence. coef(), vcov(), confint(), logLik(), AIC(), BIC(), nobs(), fitted(), residuals() (response, Pearson randomized quantile), simulate() update() work R models. tidy(), glance() augment() return tibbles broom format. Model Evaluation, Comparison, Convenience Functions regCompTest() compares model base model, two fitted models, likelihood ratio test, AIC, BIC McFadden’s pseudo R-squared. regCompTable() creates publication-ready table comparing multiple models. margEffTable() computes marginal effects (elasticities) delta-method bootstrap standard errors. cureplot() generates CURE plot specified model, based cureplots package. rootogram() compares observed expected count frequencies. mae() rmse() compute mean absolute error root mean squared error; myAIC() myBIC() compute AIC BIC log-likelihood. halton_dists(), corr_haltons() cor2cov() generate (correlated) Halton draws convert correlation matrices covariance matrices. Distribution Functions Density (d), distribution (p), quantile (q) random generation (r) functions provided distribution: Count distributions Conway-Maxwell-Poisson (COM): dcom, pcom, qcom, rcom Delaporte: ddelaporte, pdelaporte, qdelaporte, rdelaporte Discrete Weibull: ddweib, pdweib, qdweib, rdweib Double Poisson: ddpo, pdpo, qdpo, rdpo Gamma Count: dgcount, pgcount, qgcount, rgcount Generalized Hermite: dghermite, pghermite, qghermite, rghermite Generalized Poisson Version 1: dgp1, pgp1, qgp1, rgp1 Generalized Poisson Version 2: dgp2, pgp2, qgp2, rgp2 Generalized Waring: dgwar, pgwar, qgwar, rgwar Hyper-Poisson: dhpois, phpois, qhpois, rhpois Negative Binomial-Generalized Exponential: dnbge, pnbge, qnbge, rnbge Poisson-Generalized-Exponential: dpge, ppge, qpge, rpge Poisson-Inverse-Gamma: dpinvgamma, ppinvgamma, qpinvgamma, rpinvgamma Poisson-Inverse-Gaussian: dpinvgaus, ppinvgaus, qpinvgaus, rpinvgaus Poisson-Lindley: dplind, pplind, qplind, rplind Poisson-Lindley-Gamma (Negative Binomial-Lindley): dplindGamma, pplindGamma, qplindGamma, rplindGamma Poisson-Lindley-Lognormal: dplindLnorm, pplindLnorm, qplindLnorm, rplindLnorm Poisson-Lognormal: dpLnorm, ppLnorm, qpLnorm, rpLnorm Poisson-Weibull: dpoisweibull, ppoisweibull, qpoisweibull, rpoisweibull Polya-Aeppli: dpaeppli, ppaeppli, qpaeppli, rpaeppli Sichel: dsichel, psichel, qsichel, rsichel See ?count_families every distribution available countreg() countreg_rp(), parameters, variance model features. Continuous distributions Inverse Gamma: dinvgamma, pinvgamma, qinvgamma, rinvgamma Inverse Gaussian: rinvgaus Lindley: dlindley, plindley, qlindley, rlindley Triangular: dtri, ptri, qtri, rtri Lognormal: moment_lognormal moments lognormal distribution Data Three datasets included: washington_roads: sample Washington primary 2-lane roads years 2016-2018 (507 road segments, observed three years). Data roads, traffic volumes (AADT) associated crashes obtained Highway Safety Information System (HSIS). abalone_rings: shell-ring counts physical measurements 4,177 abalone UCI Machine Learning Repository (CC 4.0), non-transportation example conditionally underdispersed counts. stream_salamanders: repeated counts seven stream salamander groups 23 sites Kentucky (Price et al., 2016; Dryad, CC0), zero-heavy, overdispersed grouped site.

PMF (Type 1) : $$ f(y|\eta,\mu)=\begin{cases} f(0)=\exp\left(\frac{\mu}{\eta}(1-\sqrt{1+2\eta})\right)\\ f(y>0)=f(0)\frac{\mu^y}{y!}(1+2\eta)^{-y/2}     \sum_{j=0}^{y-1}\frac{\Gamma(y+j)}     {\Gamma(y-j)\Gamma(j+1)}     \left(\frac{\eta}{2\mu}\right)^j(1+2\eta)^{-j/2} \end{cases}$$ variance : $$\sigma^2=\mu+\eta\mu$$ Type 2 modifies \(\eta\) -> \(\eta\mu\): $$ f(0)=\exp\left(\frac{1}{\eta}(1-\sqrt{1+2\eta\mu})\right) $$ $$ f(y>0)=f(0)\frac{\mu^y}{y!}(1+2\eta\mu)^{-y/2}   \sum_{j=0}^{y-1}\frac{\Gamma(y+j)}   {\Gamma(y-j)\Gamma(j+1)}   \left(\frac{\eta}{2}\right)^j(1+2\eta\mu)^{-j/2} $$ Resulting variance: $$\sigma^2=\mu+\eta\mu^2$$

title: Polya-Aeppli Distribution — PolyaAeppli
text: Polya-Aeppli random variable Poisson number clusters geometric cluster sizes: $$Y = \sum_{= 1}^{M} C_i, \quad M \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda),   \quad P(C_i = c) = (1 - q) q^{c - 1}, \; c = 1, 2, \ldots$$ \(P(Y = 0) = e^{-\lambda}\) , \(y \geq 1\), $$P(Y = y) = e^{-\lambda} \sum_{j = 1}^{y} \frac{\lambda^j}{j!}   \binom{y - 1}{j - 1} q^{y - j} (1 - q)^j.$$ mean variance $$E[Y] = \frac{\lambda}{1 - q}, \qquad   \mathrm{Var}[Y] = \frac{\lambda (1 + q)}{(1 - q)^2}.$$ \(q = 0\) gives Poisson distribution mean \(\lambda\). parameterization polyaAeppli package. Polya-Aeppli distribution Poisson-Tweedie distribution power parameter 1.5: count mean \(\mu\) variance \(\mu + \phi\mu^{1.5}\) Polya-Aeppli \(q = d / (2 + d)\) \(\lambda = \mu (1 - q)\), \(d = \phi\sqrt{\mu}\). Probabilities computed summing decomposition number clusters log scale (terms positive); tails computed directly. Random deviates generated definition.

title: Generate Correlated Random Variables Using Halton or Scrambled Halton Draws — corr_haltons
code: # Define mean, correlation, and standard deviations means <- c(3, 2, 0.9) sdevs <- c(0.25,1.5,0.8) CORR <- matrix(c(1, -0.3, 0.5, -0.3, 1, -0.2, 0.5, -0.2, 1), 3, 3)  # Create the Cholesky decomposition matrix and set values for ndraws, etc. ndraws <- 5000 scrambled <- TRUE dist <- "normal"  # simulated the data simulated_data <- corr_haltons(means, stdev=sdevs, correlations=CORR,                                 ndraws=ndraws, scrambled=scrambled,                                 dist=dist)  # look at the mean, standard deviation, and correlation of the simulated data apply(simulated_data, 2, mean) #> [1] 2.9991697 2.0247787 0.9048085 apply(simulated_data, 2, sd) #> [1] 0.2473552 1.4834057 0.7913246 cor(simulated_data) #>            [,1]       [,2]       [,3] #> [1,]  1.0000000 -0.2942589  0.5091853 #> [2,] -0.2942589  1.0000000 -0.1922064 #> [3,]  0.5091853 -0.1922064  1.0000000  # providing a cholesky decomposition matrix dist <- "normal" cholesky <- chol(cor2cov(CORR, sdevs)) simulated_data <- corr_haltons(means, cholesky=cholesky, ndraws=ndraws,                                 scrambled=scrambled, dist=dist) apply(simulated_data, 2, mean) #> [1] 2.9991697 2.0247787 0.9048085 apply(simulated_data, 2, sd) #> [1] 0.2473552 1.4834057 0.7913246 cor(simulated_data) #>            [,1]       [,2]       [,3] #> [1,]  1.0000000 -0.2942589  0.5091853 #> [2,] -0.2942589  1.0000000 -0.1922064 #> [3,]  0.5091853 -0.1922064  1.0000000  # Truncated normal dist <- "truncated_normal" lower <- 0 upper <- 30 simulated_data <- corr_haltons(means, cholesky=cholesky, ndraws=ndraws,                                 scrambled=scrambled, dist=dist,                                 lower=lower, upper=upper) apply(simulated_data, 2, mean) #> [1] 2.999170 2.289699 1.098357 apply(simulated_data, 2, sd) #> [1] 0.2473552 1.2673604 0.6431974 cor(simulated_data) #>            [,1]       [,2]       [,3] #> [1,]  1.0000000 -0.2924282  0.4997401 #> [2,] -0.2924282  1.0000000 -0.1837396 #> [3,]  0.4997401 -0.1837396  1.0000000

title: Count regression models — countreg
text: implements Poisson regression model using Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE), opposed Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares (IRLS) method used glm function. PMF log-likelihood functions : $$P(Y = y) = \frac{e^{-\mu} \mu^y}{y!}$$ $$LL_{\text{Poisson}}(\beta) =        \sum_{=1}^n \left[ -\mu_i + y_i \ln(\mu_i) - \ln(y_i!) \right]$$ mean : $$\mu = exp(X\beta)$$ variance : $$\text{Var}(Y) = \mu$$

title: Count regression models — countreg
text: implements Generalized Poisson Version 1 model using MLE. PMF : $$ f(y|\phi,\mu)=\frac{\mu(\mu+\phi y)^{y-1} exp\left(-\frac{\mu+\phi y} {1+\phi}\right)}{(1+\phi)^y y!} $$ \(\phi\) dispersion parameter restriction \(\phi>-1\), \(\mu>0\) mean value, \(y\) non-negative integer. mean modeled : $$\mu = exp(X\beta)$$ variance GP-1 distribution : $$\sigma^2=(1+\phi)^2 \mu$$ \(\phi>0\), distribution overdispersed. \(\phi=0\), distribution equidispersed. \(\phi<0\), distribution underdispersed. Furthermore, \(\phi>-1\) required distribution. \(\phi<0\), also maximum value support integer value \(y\). \(y_max=\left\lfloor -\frac{\mu}{\phi} \right\rfloor\). account range possible values, modeled $$ln(\phi+1)$$. Underdispersion: dispersion parameter negative, PMF truncated point renormalized, mean variance differ formulas \(\mu\) location parameter rather mean (e.g. GP1 \(\mu = 0.75\) \(\phi = -0.5\) mean 0.803; \(-\mu/\phi < 1\) probability 0). Predictions, Pearson residuals, simulations marginal effects use exact moments renormalized PMF.

title: Count regression models — countreg
text: implements Generalized Poisson Version 2 model using MLE. PMF : $$ f(y|\mu,\alpha)= \frac{\mu(\mu+\alpha\mu y)^{y-1} \exp\left(-\frac{\mu+\alpha\mu y}{1+\alpha\mu}\right)} {(1+\alpha\mu)^y y!} $$ \(\alpha\) dispersion parameter restriction \(1+\alpha\mu>0\), \(\mu>0\) mean value, \(y\) non-negative integer. mean modeled : $$\mu = exp(X\beta)$$ variance GP-2 distribution : $$\sigma^2=\mu(1+\alpha\mu)^2$$ \(\alpha > 0\), distribution overdispersed. \(\alpha = 0\), distribution equidispersed reduces ordinary Poisson distribution. \(\alpha < 0\) \(1 + \alpha\mu > 0\), distribution underdispersed finite support. underdispersed case, largest possible value \(y\) bounded \(\left\lceil -1/\alpha \right\rceil - 1\), .e., largest integer satisfying \(1 + \alpha y > 0\). account range possible values, modeled $$ln(\alpha+1)$$. Underdispersion: dispersion parameter negative, PMF truncated point renormalized, mean variance differ formulas \(\mu\) location parameter rather mean (e.g. GP1 \(\mu = 0.75\) \(\phi = -0.5\) mean 0.803; \(-\mu/\phi < 1\) probability 0). Predictions, Pearson residuals, simulations marginal effects use exact moments renormalized PMF.

title: Count regression models — countreg
text: PMF log-likelihood functions : $$P(Y = y) =     \frac{\Gamma(y + \frac{\mu}{\alpha})}{y! \, \Gamma(\frac{\mu}{\alpha})}     \left( \frac{\frac{\mu}{\alpha}}{\frac{\mu}{\alpha} + \mu} \right)     ^{\frac{\mu}{\alpha}} \left( \frac{\mu}{\frac{\mu}{\alpha} + \mu}     \right)^y$$ $$LL_{\text{NB1}}(\beta, \alpha) = \sum_{=1}^n \left[ \ln \Gamma\left( y_i + \frac{\mu_i}{\alpha} \right) - \ln \Gamma\left( \frac{\mu_i}{\alpha} \right) - \ln y_i! + \frac{\mu_i}{\alpha} \ln \left( \frac{\frac{\mu_i}{\alpha}}{\frac{\mu_i}{\alpha} + \mu_i} \right) + y_i \ln \left( \frac{\mu_i}{\frac{\mu_i}{\alpha} + \mu_i} \right) \right]$$ mean : $$\mu = exp(X\beta)$$ variance : $$\text{Var}(Y) = \mu + \alpha\mu$$

title: Raw Moment of a Lognormal Distribution — moment_lognormal
text: Let \(X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)\) \(Y = \exp(X)\). \(Y\) follows lognormal distribution, raw moment order \(n\) : $$ E[Y^n] = \exp\left(n\mu + \frac{n^2\sigma^2}{2}\right). $$ particular, mean : $$ E[Y] = \exp\left(\mu + \frac{\sigma^2}{2}\right), $$ variance can calculated : $$ \mathrm{Var}(Y) = E[Y^2] - E[Y]^2. $$ function can used adjust predictions generalized linear mixed models normally distributed random parameters log link.

title: Negative Multinomial Family Panel Regression (NM1, NM2, NM-P) — negmultinom
text: Estimate negative multinomial (NM) regression model clustered panel count data. Within cluster (e.g., site observed several years), counts conditionally independent Poisson variables share common gamma-distributed multiplicative frailty mean 1. Integrating frailty gives negative multinomial likelihood closed form. Three members family available, mirroring NB-1, NB-2, NB-P forms negative binomial countreg: "NM2" (default): conventional negative multinomial. Every observation, every within-cluster aggregate, NB-2 marginal \(\alpha\). model estimated repois. "NM1": frailty variance calibrated cluster total follows NB-1 distribution. "NMP": frailty variance calibrated cluster total follows NB-P distribution power parameter \(p\). \(\ln(\alpha)\) \(p\) can specified functions cluster-level variables.

title: Negative Multinomial Family Panel Regression (NM1, NM2, NM-P) — negmultinom
text: Let \(\) index clusters \(t\) index observations within cluster. mean modeled $$\mu_{} = \exp(X_{}\beta + \text{offset}_{}).$$ Conditional cluster frailty \(U_i\), $$Y_{} \mid U_i \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{} U_i),$$ independently \(t\), \(U_i \sim \text{Gamma}(r_i, 1/r_i)\) \(E(U_i) = 1\) \(\text{Var}(U_i) = 1/r_i\). Define cluster totals reference collection \(R\) (cluster's observations used estimation): $$y_{iR} = \sum_t y_{}, \qquad \mu_{iR} = \sum_t \mu_{}.$$ three family members differ gamma shape parameter \(r_i\): $$\text{NM2: } r_i = \frac{1}{\alpha_i}, \qquad       \text{NM1: } r_i = \frac{\mu_{iR}}{\alpha_i}, \qquad       \text{NM-P: } r_i = \frac{\mu_{iR}^{2-p_i}}{\alpha_i}.$$ NM2 NM1 special cases \(p = 2\) \(p = 1\) NM-P.

title: Negative Multinomial Family Panel Regression (NM1, NM2, NM-P) — negmultinom
text: Integrating \(U_i\) gives negative multinomial PMF: $$P(\mathbf{y}_i \mid \boldsymbol{\mu}_i) =   \frac{\Gamma(r_i + y_{iR})}{\Gamma(r_i)\prod_t y_{}!}   \left(\frac{r_i}{r_i + \mu_{iR}}\right)^{r_i}   \prod_t \left(\frac{\mu_{}}{r_i + \mu_{iR}}\right)^{y_{}}.$$ log-likelihood cluster \(\) : $$LL_i = \ln\Gamma(r_i + y_{iR}) - \ln\Gamma(r_i) + r_i\ln(r_i)   - (r_i + y_{iR})\ln(r_i + \mu_{iR})   + \sum_t y_{}\ln(\mu_{}) - \sum_t \ln(y_{}!).$$

title: Negative Multinomial Family Panel Regression (NM1, NM2, NM-P) — negmultinom
text: every family member, \(E(Y_{}) = \mu_{}\). variance covariance : $$\text{Var}(Y_{}) = \mu_{} + \frac{\mu_{}^2}{r_i}, \qquad       \text{Cov}(Y_{}, Y_{}) = \frac{\mu_{}\mu_{}}{r_i}.$$ cluster total therefore satisfies $$\text{Var}(Y_{iR}) = \mu_{iR} + \alpha_i\mu_{iR}^{p_i},$$ .e., NB-2, NB-1, NB-P "NM2", "NM1", "NMP", respectively.

text: poislind_re() function poisLind.re(), name tools mistake S3 method. function poisLindRE similar poisLind function, includes additional argument group_var specifies grouping variable random effects. function estimates Random Effects Poisson-Lindley regression model using maximum likelihood. similar poisLind, includes additional terms account random effects. Random Effects Poisson-Lindley model useful panel data assumes random effects follow gamma distribution. PDF $$ f(y_{}|\mu_{},\theta)=\frac{\theta^2}{\theta+1} \prod_{t=1}^{n_i}\frac{\left(\mu_{}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)} {\theta+2}\right)^{y_{}}}{y_{}!} \cdot \frac{ \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{}\right)! \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\mu_{}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2}       + \theta + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{} + 1\right) }{ \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\mu_{}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2}       + \theta\right)^{\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{}+2} } $$ log-likelihood function : $$ LL = 2\log(\theta) - \log(\theta+1)   + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i} y_{}\log(\mu_{})   + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i} y_{}\log\!\left(       \frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2}     \right)   - \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\log(y_{}!)   + \log\!\left(       \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{}\right)!     \right)   + \log\!\left(       \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\mu_{}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2}       + \theta + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{} + 1     \right)   - \left(\sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{} + 2\right)     \log\!\left(       \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\mu_{}\frac{\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2}       + \theta     \right) $$ mean variance : $$\mu_{}=\exp(X_{} \beta)$$ $$ V(\mu_{})=\mu_{}+ \left(1-\frac{2}{(\theta+2)^2}\right)\mu_{}^2 $$

title: Estimate a Random Effects Negative Binomial regression model — renb
text: function estimates random effects negative binomial (RENB) regression model. model based NB-1 model. PDF RENB : $$f(y_{}|\lambda_{}, , b) =   \frac{\Gamma(+b)     \Gamma(+ \sum_{t = 1}^{n_i} \lambda_{})     \Gamma(b + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{})}     {\Gamma() \Gamma(b) \Gamma(+ b +        \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}\lambda_{} + \sum_{t=1}^{n_i}y_{})} \prod_{t=1}^{n_i}        \frac{\Gamma(\lambda_{}+y_{})}{\Gamma(\lambda_{})\Gamma(y_{}+1)}$$ \(y_{}\) count outcome individual \(\) time \(t\), \(\lambda_{}\) latent Poisson mean parameter individual \(\) time \(t\). parameters \(\) \(b\) shape parameters beta distribution used model random effects. RENB model allows overdispersion count data accounts unobserved heterogeneity across individuals including random effects model. formulation follows approach described paper Hausman, Hall, Griliches (1984) modeling panel data random effects. marginal mean marginal variance RENB model given : $$E[y_{}] = \lambda_{}\frac{b}{-1}=\mu_it=exp(X_{}\beta)$$ $$Var[y_{}] = \frac{+b-1}{-2}\mu_{} + \frac{+b-1}{b(-2)} \mu_{}^2$$ Thus, formulation model estimated allows use estimated coefficients directly compute marginal mean. Note RENB model panel data model, group_var argument must specified indicate grouping variable(s) random effects. model estimated using maximum likelihood estimation, optimization performed using maxLik package. user can specify optimization method maximum iterations.

title: Estimate a Random Effects Negative Binomial regression model — renb
text: Hausman, Jerry ., Bronwyn H. Hall, Zvi Griliches. "Econometric models count data application patents-R&D relationship." Econometrica: Journal Econometric Society (1984): 909-938.

text: function estimates random effects Poisson panel model. likelihood integrated analytically gamma-distributed cluster effect mean 1 variance alpha. model estimates regression coefficients one heterogeneity parameter ln(alpha).
